key_insight: A dual, bidirectional learning scheme for function-preserving weight transformations can align pretrained Transformers so they follow a much flatter linear interpolation path, making model merging scalable to billion-parameter settings.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to merge large pretrained language and vision models with reduced loss barriers, which is useful for model ensembling, transfer, and deployment-efficient adaptation.
method: Apply parameterized, function-preserving weight transformations to align functionally equivalent models.
Use a dual learning procedure where both models jointly optimize their transformations toward a shared linear path.
Reduce interpolation barriers by resolving parameter symmetries before performing linear merging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-zero loss barriers on WikiText for medium-sized language models, above 69% ImageNet top-1 accuracy across the interpolation path for ViT-L, and only small barriers for modern billion-parameter LLMs.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly learning symmetry-resolving transformations, so optimization complexity and robustness may be challenging for very large or heterogeneous model pairs.
paper_title: Scaling Linear Mode Connectivity and Merging to Billion Parameter Pretrained Transformers
